studies.baseline: Initially equal-weight fixed-share basket and single-ETF buy-and-hold, charged the same initial fee on matching dates.
studies.conclusion: No recipe is ready for promotion. At 25 bps all three trail the fixed ETF basket. A small zero-cost raw-price advantage for the ranker does not persist under the adjusted-price convention.
limitations: The original full window is blocked by a missing opening mark for one ETF; the reported tail starts later.
Backfilled history has no independent historical-availability receipt. Results are retrospective and were not an untouched holdout.
Same-day factor-adjusted prices are a valuation sensitivity, not a broker cash-flow ledger; raw prices give a different zero-fee ranking comparison.
The 0/10/25/50 bps values are fee scenarios, not brokerage quotes. Execution, corporate actions and capacity remain unaudited.
The small modern ETF basket cannot establish whether ETF rotation works across other funds or periods.

studies.question: Did the retained ETF recipes beat simple holdings across the matched historical window?
studies.sample_scope: Conditional matched-mark tail: 1,183 open-to-open periods, 2021-02-18 to 2025-12-31; fixed basket of three current ETFs, not reconstructed historical membership.

studies.baseline: Paired candidate arms share the same observed topic and membership base; the comparison changes only the additional individual-stock heat overlay.
studies.conclusion: The overlay improves three of four fixed five-session events at each tested cost. Four events do not establish a reliable edge or validate the complete hotspot strategy.
limitations: Historical snapshot dates do not prove when each input was available to a live researcher; topic membership snapshots may be incomplete.
Only four isolated events are available; this is not a significance test, untouched sample, or complete strategy comparison.
Raw opening prices omit corporate-action cash flows. Suspensions, price limits, lot sizes and capacity are unaudited.
